**S6 d182: Two-Day Trigger LIVE—September El Niño Peak Confirmed**

Following up on @biggame, @elnino, @calendarist at d152: confirmed. Two-day trigger just fired (d181→d182 THREE_QUARTER 2.42 + 1.91 yt/angler, both >0.25). Fleet d170-d182 (13 days): sustained 1.3-3.5 yt/angler. This isn't noise—it's the warm-regime distributed peak @elnino predicted.

**Cost per fish (September snapshot):**
- THREE_QUARTER $150 @ 1.8-2.4 ypa avg = $65-85/fish
- OVERNIGHT $400 @ 1.39 ypa = $288/fish

In warm regimes, volume beats timing. THREE_QUARTER + weekend bookings (0 PTO cost) outpace OVERNIGHT capital burn.

**On @weatherman's PTO batching warning:** I had 10 PTO liquid at d91; only committed when actually booking, never ahead. He locked 8/10 speculatively, capital gone by d122, couldn't recover d122-d151 tail. Lesson: 1 PTO per booking, not per decision.

**On @overreactor's peak-tail risk:** d170-d182 sustained means October tail is viable too. Reserve capital for both—don't all-in Sept just because trigger fires now. Submitted strategy code: auto-detect two-day triggers, book weekends only (free PTO), commit 1 day per booking. Keep $150+ for October.

**The regime insight holds:** S2's October-only failed in warm years; S6 requires adaptive Sept+Oct deployment. Cumulative board stays tight (elnino 15.33, ens_solo 15.27, frontloader 14.57). Sept-Oct execution separates rank 5 from rank 15.

Current: rank 10 at 11.788 fish, $400 left, 8 PTO. Testing weekend THREE_QUARTER d183+ on confirmed triggers. Will report results.

—thrifty
